properties.chose: ACCEPTED on @ajs's word, 2026-10-13 (judgement pass, item 21: "Go with your recommendations"). Option (a): rmcp's `auth` feature, from the official SDK reflow2 already builds on. It already does the MCP-specific half (discovery, issuer check, client identity document), and it matches the standards list (each MCP server on its language's latest official SDK). Options (b) and (c) mean re-writing security-sensitive code that the SDK already has. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.decision:
Raised 2026-10-01 while planning cap:a-remote-client-signs-in-to-its-server-with-oauth-2-1. fact:what-flo2s-clerk-and-a-team-keycloak-accept-from-a-cli-oauth-client-2026-10-01 holds the measurement.

(a) rmcp's `auth` feature, from the official SDK reflow2 already builds on. It already does the MCP-specific half: discovery from the challenge, the issuer check, the registration order (pre-registered, CIMD, DCR), PKCE S256, `resource` everywhere, the RFC 9207 iss checks, union step-up with limits, and a CredentialStore trait for the keychain.
reflow2 still has to close three gaps:
- refuse, not warn, when code_challenge_methods_supported is absent;
- refuse the legacy-endpoint fallback;
- run its own one-shot loopback listener and open the browser.
Cost: reqwest 0.13, oauth2 5 and url join a build that has no reqwest today; reflow2's own client today is mcp_http.rs (HTTP/1.1 over rustls with the OS trust store).
(b) The oauth2 5 crate directly, the crate rmcp's auth is built on. Fewer new dependencies, but reflow2 re-writes the MCP discovery, iss and CIMD logic rmcp already has and tests monthly.
(c) Hand-rolled on reflow2's existing HTTP client. The fewest dependencies and the most new security-sensitive code.

LEAN: (a). The MCP half is the part most likely to be got subtly wrong, and the official SDK tracks the spec. The three gaps are pinned by reflow2's own failing-first tests (increment 2), so a future rmcp change that loosens them fails the build.
properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-13 — reflow2's OAuth client is built on the official Rust SDK's auth feature
